question: Is it a sin for a couple to be alone or intimate after the nikah but before the walima?
asked: I have had my nikah done, but I am not living with my wife yet. The understanding between the two families is that we will not be alone until after the walima, a large party after which the bride will come to live with me. What if the two of us meet and engage in any type of intimacy, even to the level of consummation? Is that a sin?
answer:
Now, this is an awkward question. It's an embarrassing question, I understand, for many young men and women, but it is a question that needs to be asked.

You see, brothers and sisters, there are multiple phases of a marriage and whatnot. When a young man and woman are interested in one another and they're talking and whatnot, obviously at that stage there is nothing allowed that would not be allowed, except for a little bit more time with them to be alone in a public place. And if she wants to, she may show her hair or whatnot to him at a stage when she is comfortable to do so. But in terms of physical touching, in terms of intimacy, obviously nothing is allowed at that stage.

Now, the nikah takes place. Technically speaking, once the nikah has taken place, then in the eyes of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala they are a married couple, and **there is no sin on them, no matter what takes place after that, even if it is all the way to conjugal relations and intimacy.** Now the official nikah has taken place: ijab and qabul, the two witnesses, the mahr, everything is done. Even if it's a small ceremony, it doesn't matter; even if it's in the privacy of your house and there were five people, the family members, over, and the family expects there to be a massive festival, a thousand people come, and then the bride is going to be given away formally. But everybody knows the nikah has taken place.

In this interim, you are now between two problems, or two issues. Number one, the Sharia's allowance to do whatever you want. Number two, the family's expectations that nothing will be done. And of course, we've all been younger; we all know it's very difficult at this stage, both for men and women. It's going to be with great difficulty that they will not avail themselves of this concession.

Do realize: if you go behind your parents' back and do whatever you are doing, you are not sinful in the eyes of Allah, but there are legal ramifications and repercussions if a divorce were to take place. If no divorce takes place, then there are no ramifications whatsoever. But if a divorce takes place, then it changes the mahr amount, it changes the 'iddah. If the two of you were never alone (you had a nikah ceremony, then you went your ways and were waiting for the walima), and it so happened, for whatever reason, that the marriage ended in a divorce, in that scenario there is no 'iddah. In that scenario, the mahr will be much less. In that scenario, other things are going to come into place. However, if the two of you were alone, if the two of you engaged in any type of fondling or anything more than this, then all of a sudden, if that marriage were to end, now the divorce is going to be basically a three-month... the entire process is going to take place. Now, if that were to happen and your parents don't know that you have gone behind their backs, it's going to be a very awkward scenario for the both of you.

And by the way, that will happen if the two of you were in private, in seclusion. In the Sharia, we do not ask what you did in private; that's not our business. The fact that you were alone, such that intimacy could have occurred... whether it did or not, we are not going to ask. We don't have to ask that. But if you were alone, not in a public place, but alone in a place where intimacy could have occurred, whether you did or not, at that stage you are not sinful in the eyes of Allah, but there are legal ramifications that will affect the Sharia's ruling if a divorce were to take place.

Therefore, what I advise in this case (and of course, we all understand it is difficult) is that the understanding be made clear to the families: "Hey, look, the nikah has taken place, but we're going to be meeting up and spending the day together," whatever wording you want to use. You are not sinful, but you're going to cause some issues if, for whatever reason, the marriage does not go through and the parents thought that nothing had happened. So you have to balance between those two areas here, and you know best how to do that.

But if anything were to occur, there is no sin in the eyes of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. And the parents have the right to request (it's their right, it's their prerogative), "We don't want the two of you to be together until the walima takes place." They have that right. Now, whether you choose to do it or not... I mean, you might get them angry, but in the eyes of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala... So don't mix and match the two things here. With Allah azza wa jal, you two are married; in His eyes you are married. And if you choose to do something, there is no sin in the eyes of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. But you have done something to irritate your parents, maybe, and they have every right to be irritated. And so you have to face the music if you want to do that; it's up to you. But there is no sin on you per se.

And my advice to you is that that's something that should be conveyed in a manner that is appropriate and elegant, so that nobody is surprised later on. And Allah knows best.
